Every Tuesday, the same man walked into the same store... and touched every gift card on the rack.
He never bought one. He picked them up. Turned them over. Put them back.
The cashier figured he just couldn't decide.
On Friday, a grandmother bought a two-hundred-dollar card for her grandson's birthday.
The cashier scanned it. Loaded it. Two hundred dollars. Receipt. Done.
Eleven minutes later... the card was empty.
Because on Tuesday, the man wasn't choosing. He was sticking a barcode from his own card over every barcode on that rack.
So when the cashier scanned grandma's card... the money went straight onto his.
The grandson opened a birthday card worth nothing.
Next time you buy one... flip it over and feel the barcode. If it feels like a sticker... it is.
